# Grade 4 Sound and Vibration Technology Plan
Clearwater Elementary | 04/14/2026 | Teacher: Colleen Ferreira

## Lesson overview
Students use a short audio-visual presentation and a digital simulation to investigate how vibrations produce sound. The class has 24 students. Grace Hollis has documented profound hearing loss and needs visual access to sound information. Learning target: describe how an object's vibration affects the sound it makes. Materials include 12 tablets, one classroom computer, a projector, speakers, rubber bands, and a digital tuning-fork simulation. The simulation provides tones through speakers only; it does not display a waveform or other visual sound cue.

## Setup and presentation
Before students arrive, connect the classroom computer to the projector and speakers, then open the simulation and presentation slides. The video "Sound in Motion" is 6 minutes long; its captions are enabled. Test the speaker volume at a level students can hear from the back row. Teresa Larkin will keep the lights dimmed only during the video and simulation demonstration.

## Instruction sequence
- 9:00–9:05: Display the learning target and introduce the question, "What makes sound?"
- 9:05–9:11: Play the video, pausing once to ask students what they observe.
- 9:11–9:19: Project the simulation; vary vibration speed and have students compare the sounds.
- 9:19–9:31: Students explore the simulation on tablets in five groups of five.
- 9:31–9:40: Students stretch rubber bands and describe how changing tension affects vibration and sound.
- 9:40–9:45: During the simulation, students identify each pitch from the speaker output.

## Assessment and shutdown
Students must name one vibrating object and explain how its vibration produces sound. Grace Hollis records responses for the next lesson. Save the presentation and exit-slip tally to the Clearwater Grade 4 shared drive. Shut down the projector and return tablets to the numbered charging slots.
